shared_elements: worked stone surface with carved/incised motifs
circle or disc motif set in the upper-central area
vertical axial organisation of the design
linear border or framing lines along the edges
rows of small repeated sign-like marks
justification: The most specific correspondence is that both are upright stone surfaces organised around a vertical axis with a prominent ring or disc placed high-centre, flanked or bordered by rows of small repeated linear signs. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a bulky three-dimensional sculpted block with modelled relief bands, curved motifs and a head-like upper mass, while B is a flat thin slab bearing only thin, shallow, ruler-straight incisions and script-like characters with no modelling at all.
